translation:
Target is a proposition (with no parameters or hypotheses) defined as the conjunction of five statements about Peano arithmetic (PA) and its set of theorems PA.theory = {σ | PA ⊢ σ}:

1. There exists an arithmetic theory F (a set of arithmetic sentences) such that F is recursively enumerable and PA.theory = F.theory (i.e., the set of theorems of PA equals the set of theorems of F).
2. Every sentence σ ∈ PA.theory is true in the standard model of arithmetic (the natural numbers, ℕ↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧ σ).
3. PA.theory, viewed as an arithmetic theory (a set of axioms), is consistent (does not derive a contradiction in classical first-order logic).
4. The consistency sentence PA.craig.consistent.val — that is, the arithmetic sentence ¬Prov_{PA.craig}(⌜⊥⌝) formed from the standard provability predicate of PA.craig (the Δ₁-presented axiom set with the same theorems as PA obtained via Craig's trick, using an implicit instance that PA is recursively enumerable) — is true in the standard model of arithmetic (ℕ↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧ PA.craig.consistent.val).
5. That same consistency sentence PA.craig.consistent.val is not an element of PA.theory (i.e., it is not derivable from PA).

divergences.description: Lean cannot express the philosophical and empirical content of [P-C1] and [P-C1b]: that *our reasoning powers* may be captured by a sound formal system (the 'natural AI position'), that Lucas's and Penrose's arguments fail to refute this position, and that there is nothing *epistemically* paradoxical about humans being unable to see their own system's consistency. Target instead idealizes a reasoner's powers as a set of first-order arithmetic sentences and exhibits PA as a concrete mathematical witness showing that the abstract formal profile is jointly satisfiable—even though PA itself cannot plausibly capture human reasoning powers (since we can establish PA's soundness).

Target expresses 'nothing paradoxical resulting' only via formal consistency of PA.theory (Def4 PA.theory, which is already redundant given soundness Def3 PA.theory) together with the joint satisfiability of the five conjuncts by PA, rather than Chalmers's broader philosophical assessment of non-paradoxicality.

[P-C1b] defines the natural AI position as one 'where we cannot determine that F is sound', whereas Target formalizes unprovability of *consistency* (Def7 PA ∉ PA.theory). This matches [P-C1] ('F could not prove that F is consistent') and is a standard, slightly stronger arithmetical idealization, since full semantic soundness is not expressible as a single first-order arithmetic sentence and inability to prove consistency entails inability to prove soundness (reflection).

Target gives a single concrete instance (PA) rather than a general conditional about arbitrary sound formal systems F, and omits expectations (a) and (b) from [P-C1] (that F cannot prove its Gödel sentence G(F) and that F can prove 'If F is consistent, then G(F) is true'), keeping only the consistency-unprovability clause (c) along with soundness, consistency, RE-ness, and truth of Con.

Target restricts formal systems to sets of first-order arithmetic sentences (language ℒₒᵣ) and defines soundness (Def3) solely as truth in the standard model ℕ↓[ℒₒᵣ], whereas Chalmers's 'formal system F' and 'sound' are not restricted to first-order arithmetic.

Presentational and technical details: Def6 PA.theory existentially quantifies over an RE theory F without syntactically binding that F to PA in Def7 PA (though PA itself is implicitly RE via the typeclass argument to Def7); Def7 PA refers specifically to the consistency sentence of Craig's Δ₁ reaxiomatization PA.craig rather than PA's direct axiomatization or arbitrary RE presentations of PA.theory; and Target explicitly adds truth of Con(PA.craig) (Def2 (Def7 PA)) while leaving unrefutability (∼(Def7 PA) ∉ PA.theory) implicit as a consequence of Def3 and Def2.

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the mathematical core of the author's claim by exhibiting Peano Arithmetic as a concrete witness of a sound, consistent, recursively enumerable formal system whose true consistency sentence is unprovable (and hence undecidable) in it. The divergences are minor idealizations and omissions inherent to translating Chalmers's philosophical discussion of human reasoning powers, soundness, and Lucas/Penrose into first-order arithmetic.
